newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Serbs release four convicted Moslems.
newsitem.headline: Serbs release four convicted Moslems.

text.p: Four out of seven Bosnian Moslems who were convicted in a much-criticised trial by a Serb court on Thursday were released a few hours after their verdicts were announced, the United Nations said on Friday.
The four were sentenced in Zvornik to a year's imprisonment each for illegal possession of firearms but were released because they already spent a year in Serb custody since their arrest.
U.N. police escorted them to a bus which took them to the Moslem-Croat federation territory, said Alex Ivanko, spokesman for the U.N. police.
The other three members of the group were given 20-year prison terms for the alleged murder of four Serb woodcutters despite heavy international criticism of the court.
The court denied the Moslems' request to be defended by federation lawyers and appointed Serb attorneys who were given just five minutes to present their defence.
International officials in Bosnia called for a retrial for the remaining jailed men.
